Yes. The strongest evidence is the SELECT trial, a large randomized, placebo-controlled study of 17,604 adults with overweight or obesity, established cardiovascular disease, and no diabetes. Over an average follow-up of about 3 years, weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg reduced the relative risk of cardiovascular death, nonfatal heart attack, or nonfatal stroke by 20% compared with placebo. The events occurred in 6.5% of participants taking semaglutide versus 8.0% taking placebo—an absolute difference of 1.5 percentage points. [1][2]

Separate trials have also found cardiovascular benefit from GLP-1 drugs in people with type 2 diabetes. The size of benefit and the groups studied vary by medication and trial, so SELECT’s result should not be assumed to apply equally to everyone or to every GLP-1 drug. In SELECT, gastrointestinal side effects led more people to stop semaglutide. [1][2]
